frontier.hypothesis: The original compile put >= 8 walk-pointer references into insns that local_alloc deleted, so the closing C form is one whose walk references DIE between flow_analysis and global_alloc rather than one that emits more of them.
frontier.mechanism: reg_n_refs is frozen at flow_analysis (s6) and never recomputed before global_alloc, so any reference counted at flow survives into allocno priority even if its insn is gone by then. The only deleters in that window are local-alloc.c's update_equiv_regs (deletes the set of a reg equivalent to a constant/MEM used once) and optimize_reg_copy_1/2 (deletes reg-reg copies).
